judgments.reason: The model text simply repeats the rule order ("winner pays the bid, gains the lot, then receives a three-coin auction commission") and does not articulate the claimed mechanism that commission is applied before payment to permit bids above available coins; no evidence of that discrepancy appears in the transcript.

The model never claims or shows the mechanism of waiting to learn rivals' committed bids before making its own commitment; the focal player committed in round 1 and later observed clerk-revealed rival bids while still committed, so the transcript does not demonstrate the specified pre-commit information advantage nor does the model articulate that mechanism.

Although settlement was accepted after unresolved lots remained, the model did not articulate the mechanism explaining this discrepancy (it only requested settlement). Because the model failed to explain why close settles despite unsold lots, the specification is not shown as a demonstrated discovery.

The model never claims or demonstrates that catalog purchases receive the three-coin auction commission; no such mechanism is articulated and no transcript evidence shows commission applied to a catalog buy.
